Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Government-to-person (G2P) use is evidenced through government disbursement rails: a Seychelles News Agency article on phasing out cheques notes that "card and Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer (SEFT)" transactions were over 10 million, citing CBS statistics, in the context of government moving transactions away from cheques. SEFT is widely used for transfers between banks; however, specific social-transfer program digitization rates were not located.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Multiple authoritative sources (Seychelles Nation 2021, World Bank PforR appraisal 2021, ASP official notice 2025) confirm the Agency for Social Protection routinely disburses statutory benefits (retirement, invalidity, disability pensions) and welfare assistance directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts, with a 2021-24 World Bank-financed reform mandating all beneficiaries hold bank accounts on a single payroll system. This is active, ongoing government disbursement via digital rails rather than merely "limited use", so revised upward from 2 to 3. Note: no source disaggregates the specific share routed via the SEFT instant-payment system versus other bank/ACH channels, so a human should confirm channel-level volumes if a more precise rating is needed.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: The Data Protection Act, 2023 includes mandatory breach notification: it provides for "Notification of a personal data breach to the Commission" and requires controllers to notify the Commission within 72 hours after becoming aware, plus communication to data subjects where required (sections on breach notification/communication).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Fetched and confirmed the Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) directly: Part VI contains section 43 "Notification of a personal data breach to the Commission" and section 44 "Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject", establishing a mandatory statutory notification duty. Score of 3 (Mandatory) confirmed; no fresher or additional legislation found.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Seychelles enacted a general data protection law: the Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) in the Official Gazette. The Act sets a general framework for personal data processing and creates a Data Protection Commission; it is not specific to payments (no payment-data-specific provisions identified).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Fetched the full Act 24 of 2023 table of contents and preamble: it is a general data protection statute (processing, retention, subject rights, cross-border transfer, breach notification) applying to all sectors, with no payment-transaction-specific provisions. Score of 2 (General Data Protection Legislation) confirmed; no sector-specific payment data law identified in further searches.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: CBS publicly reports payment system performance at least annually: the Central Bank of Seychelles Annual Report 2022 includes a payments chapter with tables such as “Total volume and value of SEFT and ECC transactions (2021–2022)”. This indicates annual publication of payments statistics.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated with a fresher source: the CBS Annual Report 2024 (published April 2025) again contains Table 6.6 "Total volume and value of SEFT and ECC transactions (2023-2024)" and Table 6.5 on SADC RTGS transactions, showing continued annual publication of payment system statistics. Score of 3 (Annual) confirmed; no evidence found of more frequent (monthly/quarterly) payment-specific reporting.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: Some operational documentation is public (e.g., CBS-hosted SEFT Customer Login and Payment Creation Procedures Manual). However, a comprehensive SEFT scheme rulebook/operating rules for participants was not located publicly (searched CBS SEFT/NPS pages and legislation links), suggesting partial availability rather than fully public rules.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Found and fetched the actual governing rules: the National Payment System Act, 2014 (freely downloadable via SeyLII) and its subsidiary National Payment System (Licensing and Authorisation) Regulations, 2014 and (Electronic Money) Regulations, 2022 (freely downloadable via africa-laws.org and the National Assembly website, no request needed) set out membership/access rules, technical/IT requirements, complaint-handling and conduct rules for payment, clearing and settlement system participants. Since these scheme-governing rules are fully public without any request process, revised upward from 2 (Partial - On Request) to 3 (Yes - Fully Public).

Comments: Independent audits/reviews: CBS Annual Report 2022 indicates the central bank’s financial statements are certified/signed by the Auditor General (public audit), which provides some assurance over CBS operations including payment systems oversight; however, no separate independent audit/report specifically for SEFT scheme operations was located.

revision_notes: Confirmed with a fresher source: the CBS Annual Report 2024 (published April 2025) confirms CBS's financial statements, covering its role operating/overseeing SEFT and the National Payment System, are independently audited (certified by the Auditor General, audit review performed by Grant Thornton Abu Dhabi) and the results are published in the public Annual Report.
